findings.body: Passing `body` straight into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` executes attacker-controlled HTML in every viewer's session. A comment such as `` or `` runs as soon as the component mounts. Restore escaping or render `body` as text children; if rich formatting is required, parse markdown and sanitize with a tight tag/attribute allowlist before assigning `__html`.

summary:
This change removes the only XSS guard on user comments and injects `body` as raw HTML.

`Comment` previously ran `escapeHtml` before `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, so markup in a comment was shown as text. The new code drops that helper and assigns `body` to `__html` unchanged. There is no markdown parser and no sanitizer in the tree; any HTML, event-handler attribute, or `javascript:` URL in a comment executes in the viewer's origin.

Rich formatting needs a dedicated path: parse a limited markdown subset, then sanitize the result (allowlisted tags/attributes) before setting inner HTML — or render React elements instead of a string. Until that exists, this is not safe to merge.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removed escapeHtml and now assigns unsanitized body to dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so attacker-controlled comment HTML executes in viewers' browsers. That is a real stored-XSS regression; critical severity is appropriate.
